text: Researcher in Microsoft 365 Copilot is a specialized agent designed to handle more complex research tasks. Unlike a regular Copilot conversation, Researcher can investigate a topic across multiple sources, analyze information, and bring the findings together into a structured report with citations. Researcher uses advanced reasoning models, including GPT models from OpenAI and Claude models from Anthropic. Depending on your license and your organization's settings, you may also be able to choose which model to use. And the real value is that Researcher can combine information from your work environment with external research from the web. Let's take a look at how it works. First, I open Microsoft 365 Copilot in my browser and go to Copilot Chat. On the left sidebar, I can see Researcher pinned for quick access. I can also access Researcher directly from Copilot in Word, which is useful when I'm already working on a document and need to investigate a topic in more depth. I click Researcher to open the agent. Before starting my research, there's one important thing to pay attention to. The sources Researcher can access. Here, I have two default options. The first is Web. This allows Researcher to search for information from external websites, such as industry reports, market research, and current developments. The second is Microsoft 365. This allows Researcher to draw on my work data, including relevant emails, meetings, chats, and documents. But keep in mind, Researcher can only access work information that I already have permission to see, and that my organization's settings allow it to use. This is also why we need to be thoughtful about which sources we enable, particularly when working with confidential or sensitive information. Always follow your organization's data handling policies, especially when combining internal information with external research. Beyond these two options, I can also connect other supported applications as additional sources, depending on which connections my organization has enabled. For this demonstration, I'll use both Web and Microsoft 365 to combine internal context with external market research. Now, let's give Researcher a task. I'll paste in this prompt. Create a meeting-ready report for my board of directors on 2026 expansion opportunities in the U.S. Prioritize reputable sources, such as the World Economic Forum and BCG. Include an executive summary, key findings, risks, recommendations, and a comparison table. Provide citations for every material claim. Once I submit the prompt, Researcher may ask a few clarifying questions to better understand the scope of my request. I can answer these questions to help it focus the research. Then, Researcher gets to work. This may take several minutes because it's gathering information from multiple sources, analyzing the findings, and building a structured report. But remember, more research doesn't automatically mean the findings are correct. Once the report appears, I can review the executive summary, key findings, recommendations, and comparison table. More importantly, I can inspect the citations. I'll open a few of the underlying sources and confirm that they actually support the claims in the report. I also wanna check whether the information is current and whether any important perspectives or risks are missing. Once I'm satisfied, I can continue working with the findings. For example, I might ask, rewrite this as a two-minute verbal briefing for my board. Preserve the supporting citations and add a one-page decision table. This is where Researcher becomes particularly useful. I'm not just collecting information. I'm turning research into something that supports a business decision. I can also move the report into Word for further editing or use Co-Pilot in PowerPoint to create a presentation based on the findings. For example, I could ask Co-Pilot to turn the report into an eight-slide board presentation, highlighting the opportunities, risks, and recommended decisions. Of course, I'd review the presentation and make sure the key findings and supporting evidence are preserved. One final note about access. Researcher is available with eligible Microsoft 365 Co-Pilot licenses subject to your organization's settings. If you don't see Researcher, check with your IT administrator. There are also usage limits, which may vary by plan and change over time. So it's worth using Researcher for tasks where deeper investigation genuinely adds value, rather than for quick questions that regular Co-Pilot chat can handle. And remember, when giving Researcher access to your work data or connecting additional applications, always follow your organization's data access and security policies. Just because information is accessible doesn't automatically mean it's appropriate to use or share for every task.
